title: Paul in Corinth, Apollos at Ephesus

questions.question: In Corinth, Paul met Aquila and his wife Priscilla. Why had they recently come from Italy?
options: Because Claudius had commanded all Jews to leave Rome
Because they had heard of Paul's ministry and wanted to join him
Because a great persecution had broken out against Christians in Rome
Because they were merchants who traded throughout the Mediterranean
questions.correctAnswer: Because Claudius had commanded all Jews to leave Rome
questions.explanation: Acts 18:2 (ESV): "...recently come from Italy with his wife Priscilla, because Claudius had commanded all the Jews to leave Rome."

questions.question: Paul stayed and worked with Aquila and Priscilla because they shared the same trade. What was it?
options: Tentmaking
Fishing
Carpentry
Leather working
questions.explanation: Acts 18:3 (ESV): "and because he was of the same trade he stayed with them and worked, for they were tentmakers by trade."

questions.question: When Silas and Timothy arrived from Macedonia, Paul was occupied with the word and testifying to the Jews that Jesus was the Christ. When the Jews opposed him, he shook out his garments and said what?
options: "Your blood be on your own heads! I am innocent. From now on I will go to the Gentiles."
"The kingdom of God is taken from you and given to those who produce its fruit."
"You have rejected the word of God; God will reject you in turn."
"We turned to you first, as Moses commanded, but you refused."
questions.correctAnswer: "Your blood be on your own heads! I am innocent. From now on I will go to the Gentiles."
questions.explanation: Acts 18:6 (ESV): "And when they opposed and reviled him, he shook out his garments and said to them, 'Your blood be on your own heads! I am innocent. From now on I will go to the Gentiles.'"

questions.question: The Lord spoke to Paul in a vision and said: "Do not be afraid, but go on speaking and do not be silent, for I am with you, and no one will attack you to harm you, for I have..."?
options: "many in this city who are my people."
"appointed you as an apostle to the Gentiles."
"given you favor with the proconsul Gallio."
"sent my angel to protect you here in Corinth."
questions.correctAnswer: "many in this city who are my people."
questions.explanation: Acts 18:10 (ESV): "for I am with you, and no one will attack you to harm you, for I have many in this city who are my people."

questions.question: For how long did Paul stay in Corinth?
options: A year and six months
Two full years
Three months
A full year
questions.explanation: Acts 18:11 (ESV): "And he stayed a year and six months, teaching the word of God among them."

questions.question: The Jews brought Paul before Gallio, the proconsul of Achaia, claiming he was persuading people to worship God contrary to the law. How did Gallio respond?
options: He refused to hear the case, saying it was a matter of their own laws and he would not be their judge
He acquitted Paul after hearing his defense of the gospel
He fined the Jews for bringing a frivolous lawsuit
He asked Paul to return after he had studied the Jewish law
questions.correctAnswer: He refused to hear the case, saying it was a matter of their own laws and he would not be their judge
questions.explanation: Acts 18:14-16 (ESV): "...Gallio said to the Jews, 'If it were a matter of wrongdoing or vicious crime... I would have reason to accept your complaint. But since it is a matter of questions about words and names and your own law, see to it yourselves. I refuse to be a judge of these things.'"

questions.question: After Gallio's dismissal, who was seized and beaten in front of the tribunal, and Gallio paid no attention?
options: Sosthenes, the ruler of the synagogue
Jason, who had been Paul's host
Aquila, Paul's tentmaking partner
Crispus, a converted synagogue leader
questions.correctAnswer: Sosthenes, the ruler of the synagogue
questions.explanation: Acts 18:17 (ESV): "And they all seized Sosthenes, the ruler of the synagogue, and beat him in front of the tribunal. But Gallio paid no attention to any of this."

questions.question: On the way to Syria, Paul cut his hair because he was under a vow. Where did this happen?
options: At Cenchreae
At Corinth
At Ephesus
At Athens
questions.explanation: Acts 18:18 (ESV): "...Paul stayed many days longer, and then took leave of the brothers and set sail for Syria, and with him Priscilla and Aquila. At Cenchreae he had cut his hair, for he was under a vow."

questions.question: Who was Apollos?
options: A Jew, a native of Alexandria, an eloquent man, competent in the Scriptures
A Greek philosopher from Athens who had studied under Gamaliel
A Levite from Cyprus who had been baptized by John the Baptist
A Roman freedman who had converted to Judaism in Alexandria
questions.correctAnswer: A Jew, a native of Alexandria, an eloquent man, competent in the Scriptures
questions.explanation: Acts 18:24 (ESV): "Now a Jew named Apollos, a native of Alexandria, came to Ephesus. He was an eloquent man, competent in the Scriptures."

questions.question: Although Apollos knew of Jesus and taught accurately, he only knew the baptism of John. What did Priscilla and Aquila do?
options: They took him aside and explained to him the way of God more accurately
They brought him before the Ephesian elders for correction
They wrote a letter to Paul asking how to handle the situation
They asked him to stop teaching until he was fully instructed
questions.correctAnswer: They took him aside and explained to him the way of God more accurately
questions.explanation: Acts 18:26 (ESV): "He began to speak boldly in the synagogue, but when Priscilla and Aquila heard him, they took him aside and explained to him the way of God more accurately."

questions.question: After being instructed by Priscilla and Aquila, Apollos went to Achaia. What was his contribution there?
options: He greatly helped those who through grace had believed, for he powerfully refuted the Jews in public, showing by the Scriptures that the Christ was Jesus
He founded several new congregations in Corinth and Athens
He completed what Paul had started and then moved to Rome
He planted the church in Cenchreae and appointed its first elders
questions.correctAnswer: He greatly helped those who through grace had believed, for he powerfully refuted the Jews in public, showing by the Scriptures that the Christ was Jesus
questions.explanation: Acts 18:27-28 (ESV): "...he greatly helped those who through grace had believed, for he powerfully refuted the Jews in public, showing by the Scriptures that the Christ was Jesus."

questions.question: The ruler of the synagogue in Corinth whose whole household believed was named what?
options: Crispus
Sosthenes
Gaius
Erastus
questions.explanation: Acts 18:8 (ESV): "Crispus, the ruler of the synagogue, believed in the Lord, together with his entire household."

questions.question: When Paul arrived at Ephesus briefly, the Jews asked him to stay longer. What was his response?
options: "I will return to you if God wills," and he departed
"The Spirit calls me to Antioch; I cannot delay."
"I must reach Jerusalem for the feast; pray for me."
"I will send Apollos to teach you while I am away."
questions.correctAnswer: "I will return to you if God wills," and he departed
questions.explanation: Acts 18:21 (ESV): "But on taking leave of them he said, 'I will return to you if God wills,' and he set sail from Ephesus."

questions.question: After visiting Antioch, Paul went through the regions of Galatia and Phrygia, doing what for the disciples?
options: Strengthening all the disciples
Planting new churches in each city
Collecting offerings for Jerusalem
Appointing elders in each congregation
questions.explanation: Acts 18:23 (ESV): "After spending some time there, he departed and went from one place to the next through the region of Galatia and Phrygia, strengthening all the disciples."

questions.question: Paul had made a vow before leaving Corinth. Based on the Jewish context, what type of vow was it most likely?
options: A Nazirite vow, after which the shorn hair was to be offered at the temple
A vow of silence until he arrived safely in Jerusalem
A vow of fasting until the gospel bore fruit in a new city
A vow of celibacy until the Lord's return
questions.correctAnswer: A Nazirite vow, after which the shorn hair was to be offered at the temple
questions.explanation: Acts 18:18 (ESV): "he had cut his hair, for he was under a vow." The cutting of hair ending a vow matches Numbers 6 Nazirite procedures.

key_verse_text: "Do not be afraid, but go on speaking and do not be silent, for I am with you, and no one will attack you to harm you, for I have many in this city who are my people."
